title: Time, Work & Efficiency Principles
summary: Core concepts of work rate, efficiency ratios, alternate day working, and pipe-cistern applications.

blocks.content: Work done is directly proportional to efficiency and time spent. Assuming total work as 1 unit (or LCM of individual completion days):

blocks.caption: Work = Efficiency × Time
blocks.explanation: Where W is total work units, E is rate of work per day/hour, and T is time taken.

blocks.title: LCM Method for Fast Calculation
blocks.summary: Instead of working with fractions 1/A and 1/B, assume Total Work = LCM(A, B). Efficiency is then easily calculated as integer units per day.
details: If A takes 10 days and B takes 15 days: Total Work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units.
Efficiency of A = 3 units/day, Efficiency of B = 2 units/day.
Combined Efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day. Time taken together = 30 / 5 = 6 days.

blocks.title: Worked Example 1: Alternate Working Days & Efficiency Shifts
blocks.question: A can complete a project in 12 days, B in 16 days, and C in 24 days. A and B work together on Day 1, B and C on Day 2, C and A on Day 3, and the cycle repeats. Find the total time taken to complete the project.
given: Time taken by A alone = 12 days
Time taken by B alone = 16 days
Time taken by C alone = 24 days
blocks.method: Step 1: Calculate Total Work using LCM. Step 2: Compute individual daily efficiencies. Step 3: Find work done in 1 3-day cycle. Step 4: Determine remaining work and final exact days.

steps.title: Calculate Individual Efficiencies
steps.explanation: Efficiency of A = 48/12 = 4 units/day. Efficiency of B = 48/16 = 3 units/day. Efficiency of C = 48/24 = 2 units/day.
steps.latex: E_A = 4\text{ u/d}, \quad E_B = 3\text{ u/d}, \quad E_C = 2\text{ u/d}

steps.title: Calculate 3-Day Cycle Work
steps.explanation: Day 1 (A+B) = 4 + 3 = 7 units. Day 2 (B+C) = 3 + 2 = 5 units. Day 3 (C+A) = 2 + 4 = 6 units. Total work in 1 cycle (3 days) = 7 + 5 + 6 = 18 units.

steps.title: Compute Full Cycles & Remaining Work
steps.explanation: In 2 full cycles (6 days), work completed = 2 × 18 = 36 units. Remaining work = 48 - 36 = 12 units. On Day 7 (A+B), they complete 7 units. Remaining = 12 - 7 = 5 units. On Day 8 (B+C), capacity is 5 units/day, so they complete remaining 5 units in exactly 5/5 = 1 full day.

blocks.title: Exam Trap: Negative Work in Pipe Cistern Problems
blocks.content: When dealing with outlet pipes (leaks), their efficiency MUST be subtracted from total positive efficiency. Never add outlet capacity.
blocks.trapDetails: Net Efficiency = E_inlet - E_outlet. If Net Efficiency <= 0, the cistern will never fill.
